California State Polytechnic University, Pomona, invites
applications for a tenure-track faculty position in the Department
of Electromechanical Engineering Technology. Cal
Poly Pomona is one of three polytechnic universities in the
22-campus
California State University system and among 12 such
institutions nationwide. Since its founding in 1938, Cal Poly
Pomona students participate in an integrative experiential learning
education that is inclusive, relevant, and values diverse
perspectives and experiences. With a variety of degree programs in
the arts, humanities, sciences, engineering, and professional
disciplines, the university is well known for its learn- by-doing
approach and
Teacher Scholar Model.
The university is noted for its scenic and historic 1,400-acre
campus, which was once the winter ranch of cereal magnate W.K.
Kellogg. We acknowledge that Cal Poly Pomona resides on the
territorial and homelands of the Tongva and Tataavium people, who
are the traditional land caretakers of Tovaangar. The university's
nearly 30,000 students are taught and mentored by the campus's more
than 1,400 faculty as part of 54 baccalaureate and 29 master's
degree programs, 11 credential and certificate programs, and a
doctorate in educational leadership.
Highly regarded among its peer institutions, Cal Poly Pomona is No.
2 in the U.S. News and World Report rankings of top public regional
universities in the west and was named the No. 28 best value
college in the nation by Money Magazine. Cal Poly Pomona, a
Hispanic-Serving Institution and an Asian American and Native
American Pacific Islander-Serving Institution, stands as a national
leader in promoting social mobility, and was
placed among the 25 top institutions in the country in awarding
bachelor's degrees to minoritized students by Diverse Issues in
Higher Education. In 2022, the campus launched the Black Thriving Initiative recognizing
that Cal Poly Pomona's future as a university is linked to the
success of its Black community. More information about our
Principles of Community can be found here.
The Cal Poly Pomona campus is located less than 30 miles east of
downtown Los Angeles at the intersection of Los Angeles, Orange,
Riverside and San Bernardino counties. It is within an hour's drive
of beaches, mountains and deserts. For additional information about
the university, please visit www.cpp.edu, and for more about faculty
life, please see YourLife@CPP.
Student Population. Cal Poly Pomona is the number one polytechnic
university in the nation for student diversity and economic
mobility. Our caring and inclusive campus community is committed to
helping anyone who dreams of success achieve it. In Fall 2024, Cal
Poly Pomona served more than 25,000 students and close to 2,000
graduate students, mostly residents of California. Over half of Cal
Poly Pomona students are first-generation college students, 70%
receive financial aid, and 42% are low-income students. The
university enrolls 57% percent of historically underrepresented
students. Our diverse student body identifies as 54%
Hispanic/Latinx, 21% Asian, 13% White, 4% two or more races, 3%
unknown, 2% African American/Black, 2% International, less than 1%
Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander, and less than 1% Native
American. Forty-five percent of students enroll in our STEM majors
and our top five enrolled programs across the university include
mechanical engineering, computer science, civil engineering,
psychology, as well as finance, real estate, and law.
College of Engineering. The College of
Engineering's mission is to prepare students for industry and
advanced studies by implementing an inclusive polytechnic
philosophy through collaborative teamwork, innovation,
entrepreneurship, and professional integrity. The College offers 12
ABET-accredited undergraduate degrees and 7 Master's degrees to
over 6,300 students across seven academic departments that include:
Aerospace Engineering, Chemical and Materials Engineering, Civil
Engineering, Electrical and Computer Engineering, Electromechanical
Engineering Technology, Industrial and Manufacturing Engineering,
and Mechanical Engineering. The College is nationally recognized by
U.S. News & World Report and currently ranks 5th among
undergraduate engineering programs in non-doctorate-granting public
institutions. Additionally, it houses more than 40 student clubs
that offer hands-on learning opportunities and have been recognized
at several national competitions. We encourage a broad range of
applicants who are committed to enhancing a culturally diverse
community of faculty, staff, and students dedicated to an inclusive
campus environment.
Department of Electromechanical Engineering
Technology. The Electromechanical Engineering Technology
Department strives to be a leader in polytechnic education in
Engineering Technology, where hands-on learning is the foundation
of a broad-based educational experience. The success of our
undergraduate programs results from the solid curriculum that
incorporates theory and practice in a learning-centered
environment. Students are provided with opportunities to apply
their knowledge in hands-on projects, collaborate with faculty
members on projects. The department offers two undergraduate
programs which are Electromechanical Systems Engineering Technology
(EMSET) and Electronic Systems Engineering Technology (ESET). The
programs strength lies in being a blend of multiple disciplines and
offering a broader background to students. Since the department
offers engineering technology programs, the programs offer
significant number of laboratories. The department has 6
tenure/tenure track faculty. We strongly believe in the value of
diversity, equity, and inclusion and the integral roles they play
in achieving teaching, research, and service excellence.
Position description. The Electromechanical
Engineering Technology Department at California State Polytechnic
University, Pomona, invites applications for one tenure-track
Assistant Professor position beginning in Fall 2027. We seek
candidates with expertise in electronics systems and devices or
signal processing. The successful candidate will be expected to
teach a broad range of Electronic Systems Engineering Technology
courses as well as relevant Electromechanical Systems Engineering
Technology courses e.g. A) Electronic Devices, B) Digital
Electronics, C) Electronic Networks, D) Microcontrollers, including
updating and developing new lecture and laboratory courses in these
areas. Additional desirable areas of teaching or knowledge which
are taught or being developed in the program include 1)
Communication Systems both Analog/RF, Microwave and Digital/Data
Systems, 2) Industrial Electronic Systems, and 3) Robotics and
Motion Control Systems Design and 4) Current AI knowledge as
applied to Undergraduate Engineering Education.
The successful candidate will demonstrate excellent teaching,
scholarly activity, written and oral communication skills and is
expected to involve students in scholarly activities.
A Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, or a closely related field from
an accredited university by the date of appointment is required.
Candidates must demonstrate a commitment to inclusive excellence
and student success, as well as strong oral and written
communication skills.
Minimum requirements include:
Ph.D. or Sc.D. in Electrical Engineering, or a closely aligned
field. The degree must be conferred by the start date of the
position.
Commitment to the practical application of engineering
principles as demonstrated in the teaching statement.
Ability to demonstrate excellent teaching, and develop and
support Electronic System Engineering Technology laboratories.
Preferred/Desired Qualifications:
Academic experience and strength in electronic system,
electronic devices or signal processing.
Industrial experience in the electronics areas that will
enhance teaching and scholarly activity and help in developing
industry contacts.
Demonstrated ability for authoring peer-reviewed publications
and scholarly activity involving students.
Strong communication skills.
Application Process:
A completed application will consist of
Cover letter in which you describe why you are interested in
the position, relevant experience, how you meet the minimum and
preferred qualifications, and your unique contribution to the
department;
Curriculum vitae;
Teaching Philosophy statement (2 pages max) that addresses Cal
Poly Pomona's commitment to excellence in education (see
above);
Research Statement (2 pages max);
The names and contact information for at least three
individuals who can serve as references;
Unofficial transcripts of the highest degree earned (official
transcripts will be required of finalists);
Teaching evaluations by students (if you have experience in
teaching)
Finalists for the position will be required to:
Provide official transcripts for the highest degree before the
on-campus interview;
Provide three letters of reference dated within the last two
years;
Create a presentation showcasing scholarly work and a teaching
demonstration for faculty and students.
First consideration will be given to completed applications
received by November 30,
2026. Applications received after the deadline will be reviewed at
the discretion of the search committee. Applications accepted only
via PageUp-online application portal-for University hires.

The Department of Chemistry at the University of Texas at Austin is
seeking to hire a tenured faculty member in experimental
electrochemistry, who would also assume the role of Director of the

funding. We are particularly interested in candidates who are
internationally recognized academic leaders in electrochemistry

Description
The search committee began reviewing applications on October 15,
2026; however, the search remains open, and applications will
continue to be accepted and considered until the positions are
filled.
The newly formed School of Computing is entering a period of
significant growth. As one of the three founding departments of the
School of Computing, and as part of this growth process, the
Department of Information (iSchool) at The University of Texas at
Austin invites applications for tenured and tenure-track faculty
positions at the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor,
to begin Fall 2027. Candidates will be expected to conduct
innovative and impactful research and to teach at both graduate and
undergraduate levels. Our tenure-track and tenured faculty normally
have a 2/1 teaching load, with opportunities for course releases
and buyouts. Salaries are competitive.
This is an open-rank, open-area search. We welcome applications
from exceptional candidates in any area. We encourage applicants
from a broad range of fields to apply. Examples of areas include
but are not limited to:
• Archives and Digital Curation
• AI and Health
• Human-Centered AI
• Human-Centered Data Science
• Human-Computer Interaction and Design
• Information Behavior
• Information Security and Privacy
We are particularly interested in information scholars whose
expertise spans more than one of these areas, focuses on their
intersections, or connects these areas to other areas of the
information field and beyond.
The Department holds the Governor Bill Daniel Professorship in
Archival Enterprise, which is one of multiple endowments available
to support appointments made through this search.
The iSchool is one of three founding departments of UT's new School
of Computing, alongside Computer Science and Statistics and Data
Science. We welcome candidates whose work creates opportunities for
collaboration with colleagues in those departments or elsewhere at
The University of Texas at Austin, including through joint
appointments.
As an interdisciplinary academic unit, our faculty are drawn from a
wide range of disciplines and collaborate broadly with other units
across campus. We welcome applications from various disciplines
including, but not limited to: information science, information
studies, computer science, data science, archival studies, library
and information science, human-centered computing, science and
technology studies, communication, psychology, design,
computational linguistics, and electrical and computer engineering.
We seek strong scholars with compelling research agendas,
regardless of disciplinary background. Applicants, especially those
unfamiliar with iSchools, are welcome to contact us prior to
submitting an application to discuss how their research connects to
our department at facultysearch@ischool.utexas.edu. See resources
from the international iSchools organization for additional
background.
Research Resources and Context
Faculty hired through this search will find substantial resources
and collaborators at UT Austin, within the School of Computing, and
within the Department.
UT Austin has a world-class reputation for AI research and
education. The university's online MS in Artificial Intelligence is
the largest AI program at any tier-one university, complementing
existing online master's programs in computer science and data
science. The Center for Generative AI hosts the largest academic
GPU cluster in the world and includes one of our faculty members on
its team. The Texas Advanced Computing Center provides world-class
AI compute resources and received a $457M award from the National
Science Foundation to create a new leadership-class computing
facility. UT also leads the $20M NSF AI Institute for Foundations
of Machine Learning, the $20M NSF-Simons AI Institute for Cosmic
Origins, and the $30M NSF Center for Human and Robot Co-Adaptation.
All three involve our faculty.
Health is among the most active areas of AI work at UT Austin. Dell
Medical School launched a new Department of Quantitative and
Systems Health Sciences in August 2026, integrating artificial
intelligence, data science, and systems-level approaches to advance
discovery and health care innovation. Dell Med, the School of
Nursing, the School of Social Work, and the College of Pharmacy are
all on the same campus, and our faculty collaborate with colleagues
across them on consumer health informatics, biomedical data, and
the social dimensions of health. Strengthening these connections is
a priority for the School of Computing, including through joint
appointments.
Responsible AI is central to UT Austin's vision for these
technologies. Good Systems, the university's campus-wide
responsible AI initiative, includes more than 120 researchers
across 30 academic units and integrates technology, policy, law,
and ethics in the pursuit of societal good. Our faculty have played
a prominent role in Good Systems, serving on its leadership team
and leading its core research projects. Two of our faculty secured
a five-year, $3M NSF Research Traineeship award addressing the
integration of responsible and ethical AI throughout the
development, design, and deployment of AI technologies, which led
to a new cross-campus Graduate Portfolio Program in Ethical AI.
Additional work on responsible AI in the Department includes
research on AI policy, design, auditing, and data collection and
stewardship, including the ethical sourcing of AI training
data.
The Department's Information eXperience Lab supports research on
how people seek, evaluate, and use information, with eye-tracking,
physiological measures, and usability facilities. The lab is a
shared resource for work in information behavior, human-computer
interaction, and human-centered data science, and it is available
to faculty across the university.
Austin is an unusually rich setting for archival research and
education, featuring the Texas State Library and Archives
Commission and the Lyndon B. Johnson Presidential Library. UT
Austin is home to the Harry Ransom Center, the Briscoe Center for
American History, and the LLILAS Benson Latin American Collections.
Within the Department, our Conservation Lab supports hands-on
teaching and research in the care and treatment of
collections.
About the Department of Information
Founded in 1948, we are a founding member of the iSchools Caucus
and a founding department of the School of Computing. We work at
the intersection of people, information, and technology. We study
how people organize, preserve, and trust information; how
technology meets the people who use it; and how computing and
society shape one another.
We offer BA and BS degrees in Informatics, an ALA-accredited Master
of Science in Information Studies, a Master of Science in
Information Security and Privacy offered jointly with the UT Center
for Identity, and a PhD in Information Studies.
About the School of Computing
Computing is bigger than any one discipline, and the biggest
breakthroughs happen where technology, data, and people come
together. The School of Computing brings together world-class
expertise, exceptional computing power, pioneering research, and
deep industry connections to address problems no single field can
solve alone. Its three founding departments are Information,
Computer Science, and Statistics and Data Science.
About The University of Texas at Austin
UT Austin has an internationally distinguished faculty, making it
one of the world's leading research universities. The university
embraces interdisciplinary research and is home to more than 200
dedicated research units, centers, and research grand
challenges.
About Austin
Austin is the capital of Texas and a major technology center, home
to 3M, Amazon, AMD, Apple, Applied Materials, Dell, Google, IBM,
Meta, and Samsung, along with a large startup community. It is also
home to substantial cultural heritage institutions, a vibrant
music, film, and art scene, and the Austin City Limits and South by
Southwest festivals. The city sits in the Hill Country of central
Texas, with a river running through its center, and appears
regularly in lists of top places to live and work.

PhD in Behavioral Analysis, Psychology, or closely related

Research program that complements or expands the department's

The College of Science and Engineering offers a variety of programs
leading to Bachelor of Science and Master of Science degrees, as
well as Doctor of Philosophy degrees in applied coastal and ocean
sciences; pharmaceutical chemistry; integrative, comparative, and
marine biology; and psychology degrees. The college also offers
combined bachelor's/master's degree programs in information
technology/computer science and information systems, computer
science/computer science and information systems, and B.S. in

jobs.description:
Job Details
Posting Details
Position Details
Title
Assistant Professor in Media, Behavior, and Health
Appointment Status
Tenure Track
Department
IU Bloomington Media School
Location
Bloomington
Position Summary
The Media School at Indiana University’s flagship Bloomington
campus is pleased to announce a faculty search for an outstanding
tenure-track colleague whose research and teaching examine the
relationships among media, behavior, and health, to start August 1,
2027.
We welcome applications from scholars working across a broad range
of topics at the intersection of media, health, and well-being.
Areas of interest may include, but are not limited to, media
influences on mental and physical health; health communication and
health behavior; social media and well-being; media representations
of health, illness, and disability; stigma and stereotyping;
cognitive, emotional, and behavioral responses to health-related
media; health misinformation; and the development and evaluation of
media-based interventions designed to improve health and
well-being. We are particularly interested in scholars whose work
helps explain how media environments, messages, and technologies
shape health-related attitudes, psychological processes,
decision-making, and behavioral outcomes.
We welcome a range of theoretical perspectives and methodological
approaches, including experimental, survey, longitudinal,
computational, neuroscientific, qualitative, and mixed-method
approaches. Candidates may study children, adolescents, adults, or
populations across the lifespan.
This position offers substantial opportunities for
interdisciplinary collaboration across Indiana University,
including with faculty in the Media School, the School of Public
Health, the Department of Psychological and Brain Sciences, the
Irsay Institute, and other units engaged in health and behavioral
research. The successful candidate will join a growing community of
scholars examining media, behavior, health, and well-being across
the campus.
The chosen applicant will be expected to maintain a productive and
theoretically significant research program, effectively teach and
mentor undergraduate and graduate students on a standard 2-2
teaching load, and serve the university, profession, and wider
community. Teaching opportunities may include courses in media
psychology, strategic communications, health communication, social
media, research methods, and other areas related to the candidate’s
expertise.
The primary criteria for this search are excellence in research and
teaching related to media, behavior, and health. Evidence of
potential to secure external funding is viewed
favorably. External funding is conceived broadly to include
government, industry, foundation, and other private sources.
About the School
The Media School combines a long-standing tradition of excellence
in journalism, film, gaming, and communications with a commitment
to digital and interactive media. It fosters a multidisciplinary
approach to education and research, equipping students with the
theoretical and practical tools necessary to lead and innovate in
the media landscape of tomorrow. Faculty members are distinguished
for their scholarly contributions and their dedication to teaching,
offering a dynamic environment for engaging with media theory,
production, and design.
The Media School is home to the Center for Documentary Research and
Practice, the Center for International Media Law and Policy
Studies, the Institute for Communication Research, the Michael I.
Arnolt Center for Investigative Journalism, the National Sports
Journalism Center, the Observatory on Social Media, Indiana Public
Media, Cream and Crimson Studios, the KIX Lab, and the Black Film
Center & Archive. The school serves more than 2,300
undergraduate majors in eight degree programs (Journalism, Media,
Game Design, Cinematic Arts, Global Media, Media Advertising,
Public Relations, and Sports Media). It also offers graduate
degrees (M.S. and Ph.D.) to approximately 75 graduate students, of
whom two-thirds are in a doctoral program. Our state-of-the-art
facilities include equipment for television, film and audio
production, game design, and communication research.
University and Community Setting
Nestled in the lively community of Bloomington, our university
campus is renowned for its stunning limestone architecture and
scenic natural landscapes. This setting fosters a culture that
values both the arts and sciences and provides substantial
opportunities for interdisciplinary research and
collaboration.
Bloomington is a vibrant midsize city located within driving
distance of Indianapolis, Chicago, Cincinnati, Columbus, and
Louisville. Our community is small yet welcoming, a home to people
from all over the world. Bloomington features an active arts
community, with several independent music and performance venues
and one of the best university cinemas in the country. Southern
Indiana is also home to beautiful scenery, and residents enjoy
year-round outdoor activities.
Basic Qualifications
ABD applications considered, but Ph.D. in communication, media,
psychology, public health, or a related field must be completed by
the date of appointment.
Demonstrated potential for research productivity in areas
related to media, behavior, and health.
Effective teaching skills adaptable to undergraduate and
graduate learning environments.

Questions regarding this position or the application process should
be directed to the chair of the search committee, Dr. Nicole
Martins, The Media School, Indiana University, at
nicomart@iu.edu.

Preferred Qualifications

collaboration.
Demonstrated potential to secure external funding.
Demonstrated success working with faculty and student
populations from a wide variety of backgrounds and
experiences.
